## AI-Generated Fix (php)

```php
<?php

// Ensure the .env file is not accessible via the web server
if (preg_match('/\.env/', $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'])) {
    header('HTTP/1.0 403 Forbidden');
    exit('Access denied');
}

// Alternatively, configure the web server to deny access to .env files
// For Apache, add the following to the .htaccess file:
// <Files ".env">
//     Order Allow,Deny
//     Deny from all
// </Files>

// For Nginx, add the following to the server block:
// location ~ /\.env {
//     deny all;
//     return 404;
// }

?>
```

---

## Explanation

The vulnerability was due to the .env file being accessible via the web server, which can expose sensitive configuration data. The fix involves checking if the request URI contains '.env' and denying access by sending a 403 Forbidden response. Additionally, server configuration changes are suggested to prevent access to .env files at the server level, ensuring they are not served to clients.
